steps.label: Whole lead
steps.say: the voice back from the backing
steps.tip: Where the split put the lead voice into Backing Vocals (louder there than in the lead, loud enough and centred, as a lead voice is), it is moved back into Lead Vocal with short ramps at the edges. Lead and backing together stay what they were, sample for sample: the mix does not change, only which stem holds the voice. Both come back as versions of their stems for the DAW. Needs a set of eight stems.

params.label: Louder by, dB
params.tip: How much louder the backing must be than the lead for a stretch to count as the lead's

params.label: Loud enough, dBFS
params.tip: Quieter than this, the backing is left as it is

params.label: Centred by, dB
params.tip: How much the middle must outweigh the sides: a lead voice stands in the centre, a choir spreads

params.label: Shortest, s
params.tip: Shorter stretches are left in the backing

steps.label: Voice tamer
steps.say: the voice's harsh bulges lowered
steps.tip: Where the voice's spectrum bulges over its own course at that moment (a resonance, a harsh overtone ringing over its neighbours: the wolf in the voice), the bulge is lowered by part of how far it stands out, a few dB at most, eased in and out; by default only what rises over the voice's own usual colour, and nothing under 2.5 kHz, where the vowels live. What does not stand out is not touched: the overtones keep their order, the colour and the breath stay, and a ringing «s» is softened where it rings, never cut short. One gain for both channels, so the voice stands where it stood. Only the voice stems; the rest of the mix is not touched. Each comes back as a version of its stem for the DAW. Shaumarov's soothe2 and SpecCraft, taken as a hint.

params.label: Most, dB
params.tip: The deepest it lowers a bulge

params.label: Stands out by, dB
params.tip: How far a bulge must stand over the voice's own course before it is touched: lower takes more, higher only the sharpest

params.label: Colour
params.tip: Keep the voice's own: only what rises over its usual bulges at that moment (a singer's formant is its presence and stays). Every bulge: its colour lowered too

params.label: From, Hz
params.tip: Below this the voice is never touched: its vowels live there, and flattened they blur the words

params.label: Up to, Hz
params.tip: Above this the air is never touched

params.label: Voices
params.tip: Which voice stems it works on: in a set of eight, the lead and the backing apart; in four or six, the one Vocals stem either way

steps.label: Voice attack and body
steps.say: the words' beginnings and their dying away, a little
steps.tip: Two envelopes of the voice, a quick one and a slow one: where the quick one rises over the slow one a word begins, and that moment is raised by up to the attack's dB; where it falls under it a sound is dying away, and that is raised by up to the body's dB. A held, steady vowel is left as it is, and the silence between phrases too. A little of each brings the voice forward without a compressor's squeeze. Only the voice stems, each back as a version for the DAW. Shaumarov's two transient compressors on the voice, taken as a hint.

params.label: Attack, dB
params.tip: How much the beginnings of words are raised at most

params.label: Body, dB
params.tip: How much the dying away of a sound is raised at most

params.label: Voices
params.tip: Which voice stems it works on: in a set of eight, the lead and the backing apart; in four or six, the one Vocals stem either way

steps.label: Bass under the kick
steps.say: the bass makes room for each kick
steps.tip: The kick and the bass share the same low octave. The kick is found on the drum stem; the bass stem is split there, zero-phase, and only its low part goes down while a kick sounds, by up to the dB asked and as far as the kick is loud. Between the kicks, and above the split always, the bass is what it was. Needs a set with the drums and the bass apart; the bass comes back as a version of its stem. Shaumarov's soothe2 keyed from the kick, taken as a hint.

params.label: Room, dB
params.tip: How far the bass's low goes down under a full kick

params.label: Below, Hz
params.tip: The split: under it the bass makes room, over it nothing changes

params.label: Back in, ms
params.tip: How fast the bass comes back after a kick

steps.label: Ambient
steps.say: a layer of nature under the song
steps.tip: A fireplace, rain, thunder, a forest, a waterfall, a mountain river, tropical birds or a canary under the song, as a strip of its own in the DAW, with its own fader. Recordings are field recordings from the bank, looped without a seam; Synthesis is made here. It sits under the song by the dB asked where it sounds, fades in and out, and may breathe with the song; thunder strikes near and far by turns, on the song's peaks or at random. Made again, it is a version of its strip.

params.label: Layer
params.tip: What sounds under the song

params.label: Sound
params.tip: Recordings: the layer's first field recording in the bank, chosen by ear (for the fireplace, Dartington); Recordings II: its second. Synthesis only where it held up by ear, light rain and thunder; the other layers are recordings only

params.label: Under the song, dB
params.tip: How far under the song the layer sits where it sounds

params.label: Fade in, s
params.tip: From silence up to its level at the start

params.label: Fade out, s
params.tip: From its level down to silence at the end

params.label: Breathe with the song, dB
params.tip: Louder where the song swells, softer where it rests, within this many dB; 0: steady

params.label: Closer before the voice, dB
params.tip: Louder by this much while the song has no voice yet (its intro), settling under the voice over the 6 s before it comes in; 0: the same all through

params.label: Thunder strikes
params.tip: For thunder: how many strikes, near and far by turns

params.label: Strikes fall
params.tip: For thunder: where the strikes fall

params.label: Variation
params.tip: Another number: another loop, other strikes, another canary

params.label: Shareable only
params.tip: Only recordings whose own recordist set a free licence (CC0 or the public domain mark); off, a private recording may sound too

steps.label: Layer
steps.say: a bank from the shelf under the song
steps.tip: The DAW's Layer: a bank from the shelf (an instrument, an effect, a drone or field recordings) laid under the song as a strip of its own.

params.label: Bank
params.tip: The bank by its id on the shelf (GET /lab/banks)

params.label: Instrument
params.tip: One of the bank's .sfz files; empty: its first

params.label: How
options: the notes of a MIDI file
params.tip: A note held through the song, the song's key held low, or a MIDI file's notes

params.label: Note
params.tip: The note held, like C3 or 48; auto: C4 for a bed, the song's key for a drone

params.label: Transpose
params.tip: Semitones up or down

params.label: MIDI
params.tip: The MIDI file played (Notes)

params.label: Level, dB
params.tip: Its level against the song where both sound

params.label: Fade in, s
params.tip: Seconds it takes to come in

params.label: Fade out, s
params.tip: Seconds it takes to go

steps.label: Pianoteq
steps.say: a stem played again on a piano
steps.tip: A stem of the set played again by the Pianoteq installed here (your own copy, bought and activated: the Studio ships none of it): its MIDI the take's own when the MIDI step made one of that stem, else transcribed here on the CPU; each note's touch read from the stem, the pedal held through each phrase, at the stem's level and length. A lane of its own in the DAW, or the stem's version. Its sound is not for training a model (Modartt's licence).

params.label: Stem
params.tip: Which stem the piano plays; a set without it gives the first of piano, other, instrumental, guitar

params.label: Instrument
params.tip: A Pianoteq preset: an instrument you have not bought plays as a demo, some of its keys silent

params.label: In the DAW
params.tip: A lane of its own plays beside the stem; the stem's version plays in its place (the lane's version button)

params.label: Dynamics
params.tip: Each note as loud as the stem played it at its attack, or all of them alike

params.label: Touch
params.tip: Every velocity moved by this much: softer below zero, harder above

params.label: Sustain pedal
params.tip: Down at a phrase's first note, up as its last one ends; a phrase ends where nothing sounds for 0.6 s

params.label: What it plays
params.tip: The stem's MIDI may hold several instruments: all of them, or only its pianos, keys and organs

params.label: Transpose, semitones
params.tip: Every note moved by this many semitones (12: an octave up), kept within the piano's 88 keys

params.label: Pianoteq's own settings
params.tip: The panel's state: a preset of any of Pianoteq's, its small presets and the values set (HERESY 1977)

steps.say: a stem played again on a pipe organ
steps.tip: A stem of the set played again by the Organteq installed here (your own copy, bought, or Modartt's trial: the Studio ships none of it): its MIDI the take's own when the MIDI step made one of that stem, else transcribed here on the CPU, on the organ's manual (C2–C7, notes beyond it moved by octaves), at the stem's level and length. A lane of its own in the DAW, or the stem's version. Its sound is not for training a model (Modartt's licence).

params.tip: Which stem Organteq plays; a set without it gives the first it has of piano, other, instrumental, guitar

params.label: Instrument
params.tip: An Organteq preset (its own window holds every one): a trial plays as Modartt lets it

params.tip: A lane of its own plays beside the stem; the stem's version plays in its place (the lane's version button)

params.label: Dynamics
params.tip: Each note as loud as the stem played it at its attack, or all of them alike

params.label: Touch
params.tip: Every velocity moved by this much: softer below zero, harder above

params.label: What it plays
params.tip: The stem's MIDI may hold several instruments: all of them, or only its pianos, keys and organs

params.label: Transpose, semitones
params.tip: Every note moved by this many semitones (12: an octave up), kept within the piano's 88 keys

params.label: Pianoteq's own settings
params.tip: The panel's state: a preset of any of Pianoteq's, its small presets and the values set (HERESY 1977)

steps.tip: A stem of the set played again by the Airteq installed here (your own copy, bought, or Modartt's trial: the Studio ships none of it): flutes, reeds, horns, bowed and blown pads, drones; its MIDI the take's own when the MIDI step made one of that stem, else transcribed here on the CPU, at the stem's level and length. A lane of its own in the DAW, or the stem's version. Its sound is not for training a model (Modartt's licence).

params.label: Stem
params.tip: Which stem Airteq plays; a set without it gives the first it has of winds, other, vocals, instrumental, piano

params.label: Instrument
params.tip: An Airteq preset (its own window holds every one): a trial plays as Modartt lets it

steps.label: Voice upscale
steps.say: the voices' top redrawn
steps.tip: The separators work at 44.1 kHz and dull a voice's top: its air, its breath, the edge of its consonants. UniverSR draws that top anew on the voice stems only, keeping each below its cutoff sample for sample, and gives them back at the set's own rate as versions of their stems for the DAW. The rest of the set is left as it is. The bundle (HERESY 1583) draws it three times, with UniverSR, Apollo-vocal and FlashSR, and blends them above the cut as the separators' ensembles do: averaged, the loudest, or air (averaged up to 16 kHz, the loudest above). Apollo-vocal (baicai1145, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: not for commercial use) and FlashSR (Jaekwon Im, no licence stated yet) come from their authors on first use, never with the Studio.

params.label: Voices
params.tip: Which voices get a new top: the lead and the backing, or the lead alone

params.label: Depth
params.tip: From where the voices' top is drawn anew: subtle above 12 kHz, normal above 8, high above 6

params.label: Upscaler
params.tip: UniverSR alone, as before; or the bundle of three: averaged (closest to a voice's own top), the loudest in each cell (brightest), or air (averaged to 16 kHz, the loudest above)

params.label: Drawn top
params.tip: The bundle's drawn band lifted or lowered against the original below it

steps.label: TTS Voice Upscaler
steps.say: a spoken voice cleaned and its top drawn
steps.tip: For the Narrator's takes only: one speaking voice, never a song. Resemble Enhance (MIT, by Resemble AI) under the hood, in full precision. Clean takes out noise and music under the speech and leaves the voice as it is; Upscale draws the top a speech model leaves empty (Drama 3 has little above 12 kHz) and polishes the voice; Restore does both, for a noisy recording; Draft is Upscale in half the steps, for a quick listen to a long chapter. Only the top keeps the take sample for sample below the cut, so the words and stresses stay the engine's own. The voice's profile (Male, Female, Mixed Male/Female Voices, by its measured pitch unless you pick it) sets where the top begins, the de-esser's band and the lows. The result comes back at the take's own rate and length, a branch of the take.

params.label: Mode
params.tip: Clean: the denoiser alone, nothing drawn. Upscale: the top drawn on a clean take. Restore: noise out and the top drawn, for a recording with noise or music under it. Draft: Upscale in half the steps

params.label: Voice
params.tip: The voice's profile. Male: the top drawn from 6.5 kHz, the hiss lowered between 4 and 8 kHz, the lows kept from 60 Hz. Female: the top from 9 kHz, the hiss between 6 and 11 kHz, the lows cleaned below 90 Hz, a gentler denoise. Mixed Male/Female Voices: each phrase by its own speaker, joined in the pauses. Auto measures the pitch of every phrase and picks one of the three (the summary says what it found). Off: as before, no profile

params.label: What changes
params.tip: Only the top: below the cut the take stays as the engine read it, sample for sample, and only the drawn band is added above it. The whole voice: the enhancer's result as it is (it redraws the voice too). Upscale and Draft only; Clean and Restore always work on the whole

params.label: Cut
params.tip: Where the drawn top begins when only the top changes: by the voice (6.5 kHz for Male, 9 kHz for Female, each phrase its own for Mixed), or a cut by hand

params.label: Mix
params.tip: How much of the result against the take, in %

params.label: Steps
params.tip: For the expert: how many times the enhancer's flow is evaluated; more is cleaner and slower

params.label: Solver
params.tip: For the expert: the method that solves the flow; midpoint is the recommended one

params.label: Temperature
params.tip: For the expert: how much noise the prior starts from; higher is richer and less steady

steps.label: Speech de-clicker
steps.say: the codec's knocks between the sentences mended
steps.tip: For the Narrator's takes only. Finds the short low knock a speech engine's codec leaves where one of its generations ends (a breath or the room's noise dropped to silence at one sample, often with one low cycle just before it) and mends each: its last 90 ms above 100 Hz, faded to the floor; the voice and every sample outside the spots stay the take's own. In a Narrator take it looks in the pieces as the engine read them and finds the spots exactly; in any other spoken take it listens to the take itself. Comes back as a branch of the take, with a reel that plays each spot before and after and a list of where they were.

params.label: Fade, ms
params.tip: How long each knock's place fades to the floor: longer is softer

params.label: Before and after
params.tip: A reel that plays each spot as it was and then as mended

steps.label: Speech denoise
steps.say: the noise between and under the words brought down
steps.tip: For the Narrator's takes only (a spoken voice, never a song). ffmpeg's FFT denoiser with the noise floor measured on the take's quietest stretches and followed as it moves: the hiss, the hum and the room between and under the words come down by the amount set, the voice left as it is. A reading the engine made is clean already (a few dB at most); a recording of one's own voice or a lecture gains the most. Comes back as a branch of the take.

params.label: Reduction, dB
params.tip: How far the noise comes down: 6 to 12 for a clean room, 20 and more for a noisy recording (more may thin the voice's breath)

steps.label: Speech de-esser
steps.say: the hiss of s and sh lowered
steps.tip: For the Narrator's takes only. Where the hiss of an s, a sh or a ts rises over the voice's body (150 Hz to 4 kHz) past the threshold, only its band (from the frequency set up to 11 kHz) comes down, four to one, its depth at most, at once and let go in 60 ms; the voice below the band passes as it was. The summary says how often it took and how deep. Comes back as a branch of the take.

params.label: Threshold, dB
params.tip: How far the hiss may rise over the voice's body before it is lowered: lower takes more, higher only the sharpest

params.label: Depth, dB
params.tip: The most the hiss band comes down

params.label: From
params.tip: Where the hiss band begins: 4 kHz for a low voice, 6 kHz for a high one

steps.label: Speech EQ
steps.say: the voice's colour set by a preset
steps.tip: For the Narrator's takes only. Clear: the rumble under 80 Hz out, the mud at 250 Hz down 2 dB, the presence at 3.5 kHz up 2 dB, air above 10 kHz up 1.5 dB. Warm: a fuller low end and a softer presence. Broadcast: the radio voice, its mud out and its presence forward. Rumble: only the rumble out. Amount scales every band but the rumble filter. Put Speech loudness after it: the EQ moves the level. Comes back as a branch of the take.

params.label: Preset
params.tip: The colour of the voice: clear for most readings, warm for a low or a tender one, broadcast for a voice that must cut through

params.label: Amount
params.tip: Every band of the preset scaled by this, the rumble filter always whole: 0.5 is half of it

steps.label: Speech loudness
steps.say: the reading to a speech loudness, its peaks under the ceiling
steps.tip: For the Narrator's takes only. The take brought to a speech loudness: −16 LUFS as podcasts by default, −18 or −19 for a quieter listening, −14 for video platforms, −23 for broadcast (EBU R128); its true peak held under the ceiling by a limiter and checked by an independent meter. A reading of the Narrator is joined to −16 LUFS already: this is the last step after the others moved its level. Comes back as a branch of the take.

params.label: Loudness
params.tip: The integrated loudness the reading is brought to

params.label: Ceiling, dBTP
params.tip: No true peak passes this

steps.label: Before and after
steps.say: any two sounds measured against each other
steps.tip: This file (after) against what it was made from, or against any file of the tree or another take chosen as Before: a print through gear, a mix against its master, a reference. Both found where they meet (a print through a loop comes back late) and compared at equal loudness: loudness, true peak, peak over loudness, loudness range, crest, width, correlation, left against right, clipped runs; the spectrograms of both and their difference (red louder after, blue quieter); the average spectra and their difference; the dynamics (what the loud moments and the sharpest peaks lost); what no filter makes from the before (distortion, noise, pumping); a verdict in words. Pictures and a page in the tree. The take itself, with no Before chosen, is measured alone.

params.label: Before
params.tip: What this file is held against: what it was made from, or any file of this take's tree, or another take (an import: a print through gear, a reference)

steps.label: Match to a reference
steps.say: its tone toward another's
steps.tip: A file's tone moved toward a reference's, loudness left out: both spectra smoothed, the difference weighted by how sure each band is, peak bands added one at a time where the most is left and refined together, each kept only if it helps and stays within the bound. The bands are the DAW's own (frequency, gain, Q), listed for its master EQ; the file is the same EQ rendered, as loud as it came or as the reference, never over −1 dBTP. The reference: a file of this take's tree or another take.

params.label: Reference
params.tip: The sound to move toward: a file of this take's tree or another take

params.label: Amount, %
params.tip: How much of the difference to take: half is a nudge, all of it a copy of the reference's tone

params.label: At most, dB
params.tip: No band moves more than this

params.label: Bands
params.tip: The DAW's master EQ holds eight

params.label: Loudness
params.tip: The result as loud as this file was, or as the reference

steps.label: Details up
steps.say: the quiet details lifted, the loudness kept
steps.tip: Three bands, split zero-phase so they sum back exactly. In each, the quiet moments are raised toward the band's own loud level, the quieter the more, up to the most asked; the loud moments are not pushed down at all, and the floor and the hiss (40 dB under) are left. Mixed in at the share asked, ten per cent as Shaumarov uses OTT, then the file is brought back to the loudness it came at: what changes is the detail under the loud parts, not the level.

params.label: Amount, %
params.tip: How much of the lifted sound goes into the file

params.label: Most, dB
params.tip: The most a band's quiet moment is raised before mixing in

steps.label: Mono Maker
steps.say: the lows in the middle
steps.tip: Below the frequency the side (L − R) is taken out, as much as asked; above it nothing changes. The side is high-passed with a zero-phase filter and the mid left as it is, so the bass and the kick sit in the centre and the stereo stays where it lives. Shaumarov's first tool on the instrument bus and the master.

params.label: Below, Hz
params.tip: The frequency under which the stereo goes to the middle

params.label: Amount, %
params.tip: How much of the side under it goes: all of it, or a part

steps.label: Peak glue
steps.say: the loud moments shaved, the loudness kept
steps.tip: A gentle compressor before anything else, as Shaumarov prepares a voice or a mix: only the loud moments lose the dB asked (its threshold found for that), the sharpest transients pass, and the file comes back as loud as it came. No ceiling here: put the True-peak ceiling at the end of the way.

params.label: Shave, dB
params.tip: How much the loud moments lose

params.label: Attack, ms
params.tip: How fast it takes hold: slower lets more of the transients through

params.label: Release, ms
params.tip: How fast it lets go

steps.label: True-peak ceiling
steps.say: the last step: no peak over the ceiling
steps.tip: An oversampled lookahead limiter, its ceiling checked by a true-peak meter. «as it came» only catches the overs at the file's own loudness; a loudness target drives into it (at most 6 dB of limiting). Shaumarov ends the master at about −0.5 dBTP.

params.label: Ceiling, dBTP
params.tip: No peak over it, between the samples too

params.label: Loudness
params.tip: The file's own loudness, or a target to drive to

pipelines.name: Narration: the speech chain
pipelines.say: de-clicked, denoised, de-essed, the voice's colour, −16 LUFS
pipelines.tip: For the Narrator's takes only: the codec's knocks between the sentences mended, the noise between the words down 10 dB, the hiss of s and sh lowered, the clear speech EQ, the reading brought to −16 LUFS under −1 dBTP, then before and after side by side.
